items.originalTitle: Custom skills, agents, and MCP servers in usage metrics API

en.title: Custom skills, agents, and MCP servers in usage metrics API
en.summary: Copilot usage metrics now show the names of the skills, custom agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, slash commands, and plugins that your organization creates, instead of grouping them under other or custom .
en.details:
Copilot usage metrics now show the names of the skills, custom agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, slash commands, and plugins that your organization creates, instead of grouping them under other or custom . This builds on the agentic CLI customization metrics released in September.

What’s new

- Named entries: In enterprise and organization reports, including per-user 1-day and 28-day reports, aggregated 1-day reports, and day_totals in aggregated 28-day reports, the totals_by_skill , totals_by_custom_agent , totals_by_mcp , totals_by_slash_cmd , and totals_by_plugin arrays now show the configured name of a customer-defined item instead of other or custom .

- More entries: Each totals_by_* list now includes up to 25 entries per record, up from five, so you can see more of the long tail of customizations your developers use. Any remaining activity is combined into a trailing other entry.

- Unchanged counts: interaction_count and the distinct_*_use_count fields are calculated the same way as before.

Why this matters

The customizations that matter most to an organization are often the ones its own teams build. Administrators can now see which internal skills, custom agents, and MCP servers developers actually use, track adoption after rolling out a new one, and focus enablement where it is needed.

items.originalTitle: Global default for Copilot features generally available

en.title: Global default for Copilot features generally available
en.summary: In September, we announced a global default policy for generally available GitHub Copilot features and supported client capabilities on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans.
en.details:
In September, we announced a global default policy for generally available GitHub Copilot features and supported client capabilities on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise plans. Starting today, we’re gradually rolling out enforcement of the policy through October 26, so it may take effect at different times for different enterprises and organizations. Eligible features left unconfigured will be set according to the global policy. Administrators can still make explicit choices for individual features at any time.

The policy applies to eligible settings on “Features & clients” and “MCP servers in Copilot”. You can review your setting under AI Controls → Copilot → Default policy for new features . For eligibility and exceptions, see the documentation on default availability .

What’s changing

Once the policy takes effect for your enterprise or organization:

- Eligible generally available features and capabilities left Unconfigured will be set according to the selected global default of Enabled , Disabled , or Let organizations decide . This is a one-time change. Subsequent changes to the default policy won’t change feature policies that are already set.

- Explicit choices are preserved. If you’ve enabled or disabled an individual feature, the rollout won’t change that setting. …

en.title: Leading European Financial Services Organizations Embrace Open Models to Build Proprietary Intelligence
en.summary: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure.
en.details:
At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure.

Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x.

“Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.”

items.originalTitle: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck

en.title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
en.summary: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack.
en.details:
Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem.

Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues.

One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity.

Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together:

- NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground.

- NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets.

- NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. …

en.details:
European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin.

Frontier Results With Open Models

Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D.

Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it.

items.originalTitle: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects

en.title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects
en.summary: Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control.
en.details:
Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control.

Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant.

NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure.

Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages.
